items.summary: Recommendation: preserve containment, authorize no new spend, and reject revenue, ROI, contribution-margin, cost-to-learn, or causal-lift claims this cycle. Known evidence is AI spend of $1,002.4598 for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 across 5,531 calls, with 234 errors and 39 instrumented sites. Amazon evidence covers only 2026-09-21: 6,219 clicks, 28 ordered items, 6 shipped items, and $4.92 aggregate commission under tracking ID other. The $4.92 cannot be assigned to sites; named site rows show $0 attributed income. A valid contribution margin is not calculable because revenue and AI-cost windows differ and infrastructure, hosting, registrar, labor, and other direct costs are absent. Naive arithmetic of $4.92 minus $1,002.4598 equals -$997.5398, but it is not a valid margin measure. The canonical affiliate CTA work may proceed only after capacity release, with no revenue forecast and measurement limited to registered affiliate clicks and available conversions.

Attribution quality is insufficient for site economics despite complete tracking-ID mapping: 18 named rows are mapped, but one aggregate provider row contains all $4.92 commission and cannot be assigned without inventing attribution. The minimum revenue measurement is a future provider export where every monetized link uses a registered site/content tracking ID, plus a dated reconciliation of clicks, ordered items, shipped items, and commission. Do not treat sessions, impressions, clicks, conversions, or AI calls as revenue.

Cost-to-learn is not calculable from the brief: AI cost is available, but experiment-level exposure, control/treatment assignment, incremental outcome, and attributable revenue are absent; the experiments source reports zero experiments. The minimum measurement is one bounded hypothesis with recorded treatment/control exposure, pre-change baseline, incremental conversion or affiliate-click outcome, and matched attributable commission before dividing spend by learning or revenue outcome.
